newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European shares smash records in early surge.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European shares smash records in early surge.

text.p: European shares rewrote the record books on Tuesday morning after the Wall Street bull thundered to yet another record close overnight -- its 14th this year.
"It looks like the big boys are back buying the big stocks," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co in the United States.
The 30-share Dow jumped 78.50 points to 7,079.39 on Monday after adding 56 points on Friday following a government report of solid job growth in February with little sign of wage-driven inflation.
The Dow close eclipsed the previous record of 7,067.46 set on February 18 although most other major U.S. market gauges remained well off record levels. The Dow set 44 records for all of 1996.

By midday, Europe's three key bourses were all firmer, though they had pulled back from their new trading records. London's FTSE index, Europe's biggest market, was up 0.24 percent, having been up 0.5 percent earlier, while France's CAC-40 index was up 0.6 percent and Germany's DAX by more than 0.7 percent.
In London, traders said shares were supported by renewed optimism over the near-term domestic interest rate outlook as well as Wall Street's impressive performance.
The FTSE 100 index was up 11.4 points at 4,448.8, having been as high as 4,466.3, and beating the previous all-time high of 4,440.8 set on Monday.

Traders noted renewed confidence that interest rates will not rise soon following comments from Bank of England governor Eddie George on Monday and the market took comfort from the latest weak sales data from the British Retail Consortium.
Traders said the recent batch of major British company results was on the whole encouraging, but some were still cautious of the market's seemingly unstoppable rise.
French shares were higher at midday, buoyed by strong tides of domestic capital flows, traders said. The strong dollar also swept in U.S. investors.
Traders said funds were staying in Paris equities, attracted by successive rises on the CAC-40 index, which was up 16.28 points at 2,725.49 at midday.
Germany's DAX index was up 27.02 points at 3,463.09 points by midday, having earlier hit a record intraday high of 3,474.98 and eyeing its next key resistance level at 3,500.

"We will see 3,500, and maybe today," said a Frankfurt dealer, who added that he was taken aback by the pace of the market's advance, despite continued solid earnings signals for German firms from the strong dollar.
"There is nothing around to break this momentum," said another dealer. "There is no sign here of a consolidation."
In currencies, the dollar was close to intraday highs at the European midsession after bouncing from just below 1.70 German marks in early trading.
Analysts said the fundamental U.S. ecoomic backdrop remained bullish for the dollar and traders said it was supported by strong bids below the psychologically-important 1.70.

U.S. asset market trends also helped underpin the currency, which stood around 1.7060 marks against 1.7027 late on Monday, having touched an overnight low of 1.6975. Chartists saw strong support at 1.6975, from a three-month-old rising trendline.

"The dollar is still hovering around and it's still looking pretty weak, but strong bids pushed it up above those levels (1.70) and that sentiment has gone across the dollar board," said Stewart Newnham, market economist at First Chicago here.
Some dealers said that overnight dollar weakness merely constituted a continued technical correction and a period of consolidation after fresh 34-month highs were scaled last week.

Concerns over the launch date of EMU have also been a cap on dollar/mark recently. But a series of Bundesbank comments late Monday in favour of EMU starting on time acted to undermine mark support in Europe.

"The economic fundamentals and interest rate outlook as well as the strength of the Dow still all point to a higher dollar," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London. Moreover, "the Bundesbank are clearly now acting together to calm market fears of an EMU delay."
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7060 marks and 121.80 yen compared with 1.7027 marks and 121.74 yen in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 11.4 points at 4,448.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 16.28 points at 2,725.49.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 27.02 points at 3,463.09 points.
PRECIOUS METALS 1200 GMT
Gold fixed at $352.60 an ounce after closing at $350.75 in London on Monday.
